landing.title: jesh
landing.subtitle: A modern Unix shell written in Rust
landing.description: Fast, POSIX-compatible, with modern features like autocomplete, syntax highlighting, and a powerful scripting language.
landing.warning: jesh is still in active development. Some Bash features may not be fully supported yet.

intelligentHistory.title: Intelligent History
intelligentHistory.desc: JSONL persistence, real-time sync across terminals, directory-aware, history pin/unpin.

autosuggestions.title: Fish-style Autosuggestions
autosuggestions.desc: Ranked by frequency, recency, directory, and pinned status. Accept with → or End.

fuzzySearch.title: Fuzzy Reverse Search
fuzzySearch.desc: Interactive Ctrl+R with substring/fuzzy matching and arrow key navigation.

fastParser.title: Fast Parser
fastParser.desc: Pipes, redirects, heredocs, process substitution, arithmetic expansion, brace expansion, extglob.

richPrompt.title: Rich Prompt
richPrompt.desc: RPROMPT, transient prompt, async git branch, theme system, Nerd Fonts, OSC 7/133.

tabCompletion.title: Tab Completion
tabCompletion.desc: TUI menu, fuzzy matching, programmable via complete -W/-F, flag descriptions.

builtins.title: 30+ Builtins
builtins.desc: cd, pushd/popd/dirs, declare/typeset, local, readonly, getopts, read, printf, and more.

terminalProtocols.title: Terminal Protocols
terminalProtocols.desc: Kitty Graphics Protocol, OSC 8 hyperlinks, OSC 133 shell integration, East Asian Width.

bashFallback.title: Bash Fallback
bashFallback.desc: Scripts with nvm, rvm and other Bash-specific features are delegated transparently.

crossPlatform.title: Cross-platform
crossPlatform.desc: Linux, macOS, Windows (native, not just WSL).

quickStart.title: Quick Start
quickStart.configExample:
# jesh configuration
INIT_INFO=true
THEME="jesh-dracula"

alias ll="eza -la"
alias gs="git status"
quickStart.runJesh: Run jesh and start typing. Press Ctrl+R for fuzzy history search, Tab for completions, and → to accept autosuggestions.

installation.sourceCmd: git clone https://github.com/jefferson-it/jesh && cd jesh && cargo build --release

gettingStarted.title: Getting Started

installation.title: Installation
installation.curlDesc: Downloads and installs the latest pre-built binary to ~/.local/bin. Requires curl and a POSIX shell.
installation.cargoDesc: This will download the source, compile it, and place the jesh binary in your ~/.cargo/bin directory. Make sure that directory is on your $PATH.
installation.sourceCmd:
git clone https://github.com/jefferson-it/jesh.git
cd jesh
cargo build --release
installation.binaryNote: The resulting binary will be at target/release/jesh. You can copy it anywhere on your $PATH.

firstSteps.title: First Steps
firstSteps.step1: Start jesh by running jesh in your terminal
firstSteps.step3: Configure your shell with jesh --init to generate config files

configuration.title: Configuration
configuration.desc: jesh looks for configuration in ~/.config/jesh/config.toml. Run jesh --init to generate a default configuration file.

basicUsage.title: Basic Usage
basicUsage.desc: jesh behaves like a standard Unix shell. Type a command and press <kbd>Enter</kbd> to execute it. Pipes, redirects, and environment variables all work as expected:
basicUsage.examples:
~> ls -la | grep ".rs"
~> echo "Hello, $USER" > greeting.txt
~> cd projects && make

completion.title: Tab Completion
completion.desc: Press Tab to complete commands, file paths, and arguments. If there are multiple matches, a TUI menu appears. Use the arrow keys to navigate the menu and Enter to select. The completion system is programmable via the complete builtin.

history.title: History Navigation
history.desc: Press Up and Down to scroll through previous commands. jesh's history is persisted to disk in JSONL format at ~/.local/share/jesh/history.jsonl and supports directory-aware filtering, pinning, and real-time sync across terminal sessions.

reverseSearch.title: Reverse Search
reverseSearch.desc: Press <kbd>Ctrl+R</kbd> to enter interactive reverse search. Start typing any portion of a previous command; jesh performs fuzzy/substring matching and displays results ranked by frequency, recency, and directory relevance. Use <kbd>Ctrl+R</kbd> again to cycle through older matches, or use the arrow keys to navigate the list. Press <kbd>Enter</kbd> to execute the selected command or <kbd>Tab</kbd> to place it on the input line for editing.

autosuggestions.title: Autosuggestions
autosuggestions.desc: As you type, jesh displays a dimmed suggestion based on your history. Press <kbd>→</kbd> (right arrow) or <kbd>End</kbd> to accept the suggestion. This feature is inspired by Fish and uses the same ranking algorithm as the reverse search.

gettingStarted.nextSteps: Read the Configuration page to customize your shell, explore the Builtins reference for the full command list, and check Scripting if you want to write jesh scripts.

scripting.intro: jesh features a modern scripting language with familiar syntax and powerful features.

parser.title: Parser
